extracted.intended_audience: young readers and novice youth rowers / club members
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt of a juvenile/children's fiction narrative that embeds practical instructions and rules for forming a boys' boat club and for basic rowing, boat discipline, and safety. Contains both social/club regulations and step‑by‑step rowing commands and technique explained by an instructor character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club constitution and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: "You must make a kind of constitution; that is, some regulations for the government of the club."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The club should adopt a written constitution/regulations governing membership and behavior. Elements mentioned or implied: selection/invitation of members, meeting times (e.g., "Two o'clock"), club-room/boathouse and library for meetings, winter indoor meetings for instruction and amusement. The constitution is to be made by the boys themselves (learning opportunity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required officer roles: clerk and coxswain (election by vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the first place, you will want a clerk and a coxswain... You will choose him by vote, as well as the clerk."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and elect officers: a clerk (record/administrative duties) and a coxswain who 'steers the boat, and has the command' (acts as captain/meeting chairman). Election by vote is specified (democratic selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral code / moral aims
rubrics_metrics.description: "You must have no profanity, no lying, no vulgar language; and no boy must be permitted to neglect his school, or his duties at home, on account of the boat."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear conduct rules: prohibit profanity, lying, and vulgar language; ensure boating activities do not cause neglect of schoolwork or household duties. The club is explicitly intended as "a society for the promotion of your moral welfare, as well as a means of amusement." This frames the club's purpose beyond recreation (moral improvement, instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boarding and launch discipline / safe embarkation
rubrics_metrics.description: "When you get into the boat, step easy, and keep quiet in your places... One at a time, and each of you take one of the seats."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict boarding procedure: do not rush or huddle into the boat; enter one at a time, step carefully, keep still once seated. Avoid standing on keel on sand (boat can tip); do not overload one side (trim ship); attend to fending off and use boat-hooks when required. Anti-patterns: jumping in together, rushing, crowding to one side; these lead to capsizing and danger (as shown by the upturning incident).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipshape order and discipline as a training principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated admonitions: "We don't want any hurrying and tumbling about... Do everything calm[ly]... you'll never larn anything if you don't go to work shipshape."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline and calm, methodical practice is emphasized as the means to learn and maintain safety. Instructor enforces repetitive drilling until movements are 'shipshape.' Implicit scoring: repetition and precision (no straggling oars, unity of motion) are markers of proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boat terminology and parts (vocabulary to be learned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions given in text: "The for'd part of the boat is the bow; ... The after part... is the starn-sheets. The middle of the boat is the waist... An oar has three parts... the blade, the loom, and the handle... thwarts... gunwale... rowlock..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners must learn the standard vocabulary: bow, stern/starn-sheets, waist, thwarts (seats), blade/loom/handle of oar, gunwale, rowlocks, tiller/tiller-ropes, grapnel (anchor). Correct use of terms underpins correct action and commands; teacher recommends writing down unfamiliar terms. Misunderstanding terms (e.g., starboard relative to facing forward) can cause confusion and mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oar handling fundamentals and stroke technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and cautions such as: "At this order, you will pick up your oars, and hold them up straight, with the blades athwartships... Drop the end of the oar into the water till the blade is just covered, no deeper. Then pause a bit, and pull the handle towards you to your breasts... You are not to bury your oar in the water above the blade at any time. You must keep the flat part of the oar up and down in the water always."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key technical points: pick up ('Up oars') cleanly and uniformly; ship oars into rowlocks without hitting the gunwale; place blade just covered (not too deep); take time and pull to chest; maintain blade vertical during stroke (don't twist so blade dives or shoots up). Instructor drills these until consistent. Anti-patterns: spearing eels (burying oar), turning blade while pulling, hitting gunwale, unsynchronized or uneven strokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands, coordinated manoeuvres, and their meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: List of commands and their described effects: 'Up oars', 'Let fall', 'Give way together', 'Stand by to lay on your oars', 'Oars!', 'Hold water', 'Stern all' (backwards), 'Starboard oars--back! Port oars--ahead!', 'Stand by to trail' / 'Trail', 'Way enough', 'In bows', 'Stand by to toss' / 'Toss'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding and executing standard boat commands in precise sequence is essential for coordinated rowing and safety. Each command has a specific timing and expected unified response (e.g., 'Let fall' — oars drop into water simultaneously; 'Give way together' — take timing from stroke, pull together; 'Hold water' — level and feather to check headway; 'Stern all' — pull backwards to back the boat; 'Trail' — let loom drag alongside). The text emphasizes timing (giving commands at beginning of stroke) and unity (no straggling oars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maneuvers for stopping, turning, and tight navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and commands for slowing/stopping and tight handling: 'Stand by to lay on your oars' + 'Oars!' to feather without touching water; 'Hold water' then 'Stern all' to back; 'Starboard oars--back! Port oars--ahead!' to spin; 'Trail' for narrow passages; 'Way enough' and 'Toss' for landing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical skills: use holding/backing/paired opposing strokes to control heading and speed; trail oars to pass narrow spots; approach landing with 'Way enough' and 'Toss' to synchronize boathooking and docking. The instructor practices each maneuver repeatedly, including emergency use (e.g., quick 'Stern all' to avoid collision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boarding/landing and boathouse procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Landing procedure: when coxswain says 'Way enough!' crew ceases rowing and 'toss the oars' and boat the oars in concert; 'In bows' to prepare going into boathouse or alongside vessel; fending with boat-hook; use of grapnel anchor when holding position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination at landing: coxswain/crew must time toss/boating of oars together; bowmen take boat-hook to fend off; use anchors/graphnel to hold position when waiting. Proper procedure avoids collisions and ensures tidy stowage (oars on thwarts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag etiquette and formal salutations
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions: placement of flags ('The blue silk one... goes in the bow... American flag... goes in the starn'), and saluting a superior officer by tossing oars ('When a boat in the navy is to meet or pass one containing a superior officer, it is the fashion to salute him with a toss of the oars...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Etiquette: assign and mount flags in prescribed sockets (bow vs stern), and perform formal 'toss of the oars' as salute to dignitaries. Also social rituals like cheers and singing mark group cohesion; instructor models patri­otic/formal behavior (three cheers, 'long may it wave').

rubrics_metrics.name: Training methods: rehearsal, incremental learning, and instructor correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout: Uncle Ben compels repetition (half-hour drills), demonstrates moves, has individuals and small groups practice, praises improvement ('Glad to hear it, youngsters... you have been very near perfect'), and recommends writing down unfamiliar material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective pedagogy: instructor demonstration, incremental practice (individual → small group → full crew), repeated drilling until uniformity, mental rehearsal ('dummy rehearsals'), and corrective feedback. Implicit metric of success: unity, absence of straggling oars, correct timing, and safety (no capsizing).
